s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan sites in Uttar Pradesh:
1. Mandi in Muzaffarnagar district yielded a Late Harappan jewellery hoard.
2. Hulas is in Meerut district.
3. Sinauli in Baghpat district has yielded 125 graves.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: Hulas is in Saharanpur district (Alamgirpur is the Meerut site). Mandi (Muzaffarnagar) gave the Late Harappan jewellery hoard and Sinauli (Baghpat) the 125 graves.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan sites in Haryana:
1. Rakhigarhi is in Hisar district.
2. Banawali is in Fatehabad district, on the Rangoi in the Ghaggar valley.
3. Bhagwanpura is in Hisar district.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: Bhagwanpura is in Kurukshetra district. Rakhigarhi is in Hisar and Banawali in Fatehabad on the Rangoi (Ghaggar valley).

s:
Match List-I (Site) with List-II (River):
List-I
A. Kalibangan
B. Rangpur
C. Daimabad
D. Harappa
List-II
i. Pravara
ii. Ravi
iii. Ghaggar
iv. Bhadar
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Kalibangan – Ghaggar, Rangpur – Bhadar, Daimabad – Pravara, Harappa – Ravi: A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan sites in Pakistan:
1. Mohenjodaro lies in Larkana district of Sindh, on the right bank of the Indus.
2. Harappa lies in Sahiwal (Montgomery) district of Punjab, on the right bank of the Ravi.
3. Chanhudaro lies on the Indus about 130 km south of Mohenjodaro.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: Harappa is on the LEFT bank of the Ravi. Mohenjodaro (Larkana, right bank of the Indus) and Chanhudaro (~130 km south of it) are correctly placed.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Daimabad lies in Ahmednagar district of Maharashtra, on the Pravara.
2. Dholavira lies on Khadir island in Kutch.
3. Lothal lies on the Narmada near the Gulf of Khambhat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: Lothal is on the Bhogava, near its Sabarmati confluence – not the Narmada. Daimabad (Ahmednagar, Pravara) and Dholavira (Khadir island, Kutch) are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about the early history of Harappa's discovery:
1. Charles Masson described the ruins of Harappa in 1826.
2. Alexander Cunningham visited Harappa in 1853 and 1856 and saw a seal.
3. In 1857 Harappan bricks were used as ballast for the Karachi–Lahore railway.
4. J. Fleet published Harappan seals in 1921.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 4 is wrong: J. Fleet published Harappan seals in 1912 (1921 is the year Harappa was excavated). Masson (1826), Cunningham (1853, 1856) and the Karachi–Lahore railway ballast (1857) are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about Sir John Marshall:
1. As Director-General of the ASI he directed the 1921-22 excavation campaign.
2. He coined the term "Indus Valley Civilisation".
3. He announced the discovery of the civilisation to the world in 1934.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: Marshall announced the civilisation in 1924. He was DG of the ASI (1902–28), directed the 1921-22 campaign and coined "Indus Valley Civilisation".

s:
Match List-I (Site) with List-II (Excavator):
List-I
A. Ropar
B. Daimabad
C. Kalibangan
D. Surkotada
List-II
i. A. Ghosh
ii. J. P. Joshi
iii. Y. D. Sharma
iv. B. P. Bopardikar
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Ropar – Y. D. Sharma (1953-55), Daimabad – B. P. Bopardikar (1958), Kalibangan – A. Ghosh (1953, then B. B. Lal and B. K. Thapar), Surkotada – J. P. Joshi (1964): A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ropar, found by B. B. Lal in 1950, was the first Harappan site dug in independent India.
2. Dholavira was found by R. S. Bisht and excavated by J. P. Joshi from 1990.
3. Chanhudaro was found by N. G. Majumdar in 1931.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 swaps the names: J. P. Joshi found Dholavira (1967-68) and R. S. Bisht excavated it from 1990. Ropar (B. B. Lal, 1950; first dig after Independence) and Chanhudaro (N. G. Majumdar, 1931) are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Harappan Civilisation:
1. It covered about 1.3 million sq km, more than Egypt and Mesopotamia.
2. The highest concentration of its sites is on the Ghaggar–Hakra system.
3. It has given the earliest evidence of iron in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: the Harappans used copper, bronze, gold, silver, lead and tin but no iron (they gave India's first use of silver). The 1.3 million sq km area and the Ghaggar–Hakra concentration (about 250 sites) are correct.

s:
Match List-I (Site) with List-II (Name / meaning):
List-I
A. Chanhudaro
B. Kalibangan
C. Dholavira
D. Lothal
List-II
i. Kotada
ii. Mini Harappa
iii. Lancashire of India
iv. Black bangles
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Chanhudaro – Lancashire of India, Kalibangan – black bangles, Dholavira – local name Kotada, Lothal – Mini Harappa: A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii.

s:
Consider the following names used in Mesopotamian records:
1. Meluhha – the Indus region
2. Dilmun – Bahrain
3. Magan – the Ganga valley
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
x: Pair 3 is wrong: Magan (Makan) is the Makran coast / Oman, not the Ganga valley. Meluhha = Indus region and Dilmun = Bahrain (an intermediate station) are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about the names of the civilisation:
1. "Harappan Civilisation" is preferred because Harappa was the first site found and the culture went beyond the Indus valley.
2. The name "Sindhu-Sarasvati Civilisation" stresses the sites on the Ghaggar–Hakra system.
3. The term "Indus Valley Civilisation" was coined by Mortimer Wheeler.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: Sir John Marshall coined "Indus Valley Civilisation" and named the culture after Harappa, the first site found. "Sindhu-Sarasvati" stresses the Ghaggar–Hakra sites.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Rakhigarhi is the largest Harappan site in India and Dholavira the second largest.
2. Harappa is the largest Harappan site in Pakistan.
3. Ganweriwala is one of the five largest Harappan sites.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: Mohenjodaro is the largest Harappan site in Pakistan. Rakhigarhi (~550 ha) is the largest in India, Dholavira second; the five largest are Harappa, Mohenjodaro, Ganweriwala, Rakhigarhi and Dholavira.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan sites and UNESCO:
1. Dholavira was inscribed in 2021 as India's 40th World Heritage Site.
2. Mohenjodaro has been a World Heritage Site since 1980.
3. Rakhigarhi was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: Rakhigarhi is only on UNESCO's Tentative List (June 2026). Dholavira (2021, India's 40th, first IVC site in India) and Mohenjodaro (1980) are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Union Budget 2020-21 named five iconic archaeological sites, including Rakhigarhi and Adichanallur.
2. In June 2026 Haryana protected Tighrana and Mitathal under the Haryana Ancient and Historical Monuments Act, 1964.
3. In June 2026 the ASI transferred Rakhigarhi's 56 skeletons to the National Museum, New Delhi.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: the 56 skeletons went to the Anthropological Survey of India. The Budget 2020-21 sites (Rakhigarhi, Hastinapur, Shivsagar, Dholavira, Adichanallur) and the protection of Tighrana and Mitathal are correct – so only two.

s:
Consider the following statements about the boundary sites of the Harappan culture:
1. Manda on the Chenab, the northern limit, was a base for Himalayan wood.
2. Alamgirpur on the Hindon, in Meerut district, marks the eastern limit.
3. Sutkagendor on the Makran coast marks the southern limit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: Sutkagendor (Makran coast, Baluchistan) is the WESTERN limit; Daimabad is the southern one. Manda (Chenab, Himalayan wood) and Alamgirpur (Hindon, Meerut) are correct.

s:
Match List-I (Phase / dating) with List-II (Dates):
List-I
A. Early Harappan phase
B. Mature Harappan phase
C. Late Harappan phase
D. D. P. Agrawal's radiocarbon dating
List-II
i. 2500–1750 BCE
ii. 1900–1300 BCE
iii. 3300–2600 BCE
iv. 2600–1900 BCE
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Early Harappan 3300–2600 BCE, Mature 2600–1900 BCE, Late 1900–1300 BCE, D. P. Agrawal's radiocarbon range 2500–1750 BCE: A-iii, B-iv, C-ii, D-i.

s:
Consider the following statements about the chronology of the Harappan Civilisation:
1. John Marshall dated it to 3250–2750 BCE by Mesopotamian cross-dating.
2. Bricks in the ratio 1:2:4 belong to the Mature Harappan phase.
3. Kot Diji and Amri are typical sites of the Late Harappan phase.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: Kot Diji, Amri and Sothi belong to the Early Harappan phase (3300–2600 BCE); the Late phase is marked by OCP and Cemetery-H. Marshall's cross-dating and the Mature-phase 1:2:4 bricks are correct.

s:
Assertion (A): The Harappan culture is classed as proto-historic.
Reason (R): Its script has not been deciphered.
In the context of the above, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Both are true and R explains A: the Harappans could write, but because the script is still unread the culture is called proto-historic rather than historic.

s:
Assertion (A): The Harappan Civilisation is placed in the Bronze Age.
Reason (R): The Harappans used copper and bronze but did not know iron.
In the context of the above, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Both are true and R explains A: copper and bronze (with gold, silver, lead and tin) were their metals and iron is absent, so it is a Bronze Age culture.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan cities:
1. No temples or palaces have been clearly found, unlike in Mesopotamia and Egypt.
2. Standard bricks, a grid plan, streets and drains point to a civic authority.
3. The absence of palaces and temples proves that there was no civic authority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: the absence of palaces or temples does NOT disprove a civic authority – standard bricks, grid, streets and drains point to one. Statement 1 is correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about what the Harappans knew:
1. They built only corbelled arches, never the true arch.
2. The assembly hall at Mohenjodaro had 20 pillars.
3. Wells, drains and bows-and-arrows were known.
4. Iron tools were in common use.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 4 is wrong: the IVC is a Bronze Age culture and did not know iron, which came c. 1000 BC in the Later Vedic age. The corbelled arch, the 20-pillared hall, wells, drains and bows-and-arrows were all known.

s:
Consider the following statements comparing the IVC and the Vedic culture:
1. Harappan pottery was red ware painted in black, while the Vedic people used Painted Grey Ware.
2. The Vedic people used a pictographic script.
3. The stratified pottery sequence from Mehrgarh to the Harappan black-on-red ware lies below the Painted Grey Ware.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: the Vedic people had no script; the pictographic (undeciphered) script belongs to the IVC. The pottery contrast and the pottery sequence below the Painted Grey Ware are correct.

s:
Match List-I (Site) with List-II (Water feature):
List-I
A. Mohenjodaro
B. Dholavira
C. Kalibangan
D. Allahdino
List-II
i. Wooden drains
ii. Well irrigation
iii. About 700 brick wells
iv. 16 reservoirs with dams and embankments
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Mohenjodaro – about 700 brick wells, Dholavira – 16 reservoirs, dams and embankments, Kalibangan – wooden drains (and house wells), Allahdino (Sindh) – well irrigation: A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan drainage:
1. House drains led into covered street drains that had manholes.
2. The waste water finally drained into soak pits or main channels.
3. Banawali had the most systematic drainage of all Harappan towns.
4. At Lothal the houses were of mud brick but the drains of burnt brick.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: Banawali had NO systematic drainage. Covered drains with manholes, soak pits / main channels and Lothal's burnt-brick drains are correct – drainage was the most advanced IVC feature.

s:
Match List-I (Site) with List-II (Town plan):
List-I
A. Kalibangan
B. Dholavira
C. Chanhudaro
D. Lothal
List-II
i. No citadel
ii. Citadel and lower town both fortified
iii. Three parts – citadel, middle town, lower town
iv. Citadel not separately walled, inside one enclosure
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Kalibangan – citadel and lower town both fortified, Dholavira – three parts, Chanhudaro – no citadel, Lothal – citadel inside one fortified enclosure: A-ii, B-iii, C-i, D-iv.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan building material:
1. Mud bricks were used for fillings and platforms and notably at Kalibangan.
2. The standard brick ratio was 1:2:4 (thickness : width : length).
3. Dholavira, like Mohenjodaro, was built mainly of baked brick.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: Dholavira used sandstone and limestone blocks, not baked brick. Mud bricks (Kalibangan) and the 1:2:4 ratio are correct.

s:
Match List-I (Feature) with List-II (Site):
List-I
A. Ornamental bricks
B. Curved bricks
C. Radial streets
D. House entrances on the main street
List-II
i. Banawali
ii. Lothal
iii. Kalibangan
iv. Chanhudaro
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Ornamental bricks – Kalibangan, curved bricks – Chanhudaro, radial streets – Banawali (the only such city), entrances on the main street – Lothal (the exception): A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan streets and houses:
1. Streets ran north-south and east-west, crossing at right angles.
2. Main streets were about 10 m wide.
3. Doors and windows of houses generally opened on the main streets.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: doors and windows opened on side lanes, not the main streets (Lothal is the exception). The right-angled grid and ~10 m main streets are correct.

s:
Assertion (A): The same size of brick was not used for all Harappan constructions.
Reason (R): House bricks and city-wall bricks kept the same 1:2:4 ratio.
In the context of the above, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: house bricks were about 7.5×15×30 cm and city-wall bricks 10×20×40 cm – the same 1:2:4 ratio but different sizes. Keeping the ratio is not why the sizes differ.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Great Bath of Mohenjodaro:
1. It lay on the citadel mound and measured about 11.88 × 7.01 m, 2.43 m deep.
2. It had flights of steps on the east and west sides.
3. It was made of burnt bricks set in gypsum mortar and waterproofed with bitumen.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: the two flights of steps were on the north and south. Its place on the citadel, its size and the gypsum mortar with bitumen waterproofing are correct.

s:
Assertion (A): Most scholars see the Great Bath as a ritual bath rather than a public bath.
Reason (R): Harappan houses had their own brick-paved bathrooms.
In the context of the above, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Both are true and R explains A: since houses had their own bathrooms, a public bath is ruled out and the Great Bath is read as a ritual bath.

s:
Match List-I (Structure) with List-II (Site):
List-I
A. Granary of 12 rooms in two rows of six
B. Warehouse on a raised platform beside the dock
C. Seven fire altars
D. Pillared assembly hall
List-II
i. Mohenjodaro
ii. Kalibangan
iii. Harappa
iv. Lothal
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Granary of 12 rooms (two rows of six, near the Ravi) – Harappa, dock warehouse – Lothal, seven fire altars – Kalibangan, pillared assembly hall (20 pillars) – Mohenjodaro: A-iii, B-iv, C-ii, D-i.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fire altars have been found at Kalibangan, Lothal, Banawali and Rakhigarhi.
2. Harappan granaries stored the farm surplus, probably taken as tax.
3. The so-called college of priests was found at Harappa.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: the college of priests is at Mohenjodaro. Fire altars at Kalibangan, Lothal, Banawali and Rakhigarhi and granaries as stores of the surplus are correct.

s:
Which of the following finds come from Harappa?
1. Cemetery H and Cemetery R-37
2. Wheat and barley in a wooden mortar
3. A dockyard
4. A bronze chariot
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Only 1 and 2 are Harappa finds. The dockyard is at Lothal and the bronze chariot at Daimabad.

s:
Consider the following statements about Dholavira:
1. It lies on Khadir island in Kachchh, Gujarat.
2. A stadium of about 283 × 47 m lay between the citadel and the middle town.
3. Its ten-sign signboard was found near the South Gate.
4. It was settled in seven stages.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: the ten-sign signboard (largest Harappan signs) was near the North Gate. Khadir island (Kachchh), the stadium and the seven stages are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about Lothal:
1. It lies on the Bhogava, a tributary of the Sabarmati, near the Gulf of Khambhat.
2. Its dock is a brick-lined basin of about 218 m × 37 m with sluice gates.
3. Its dock is regarded as the world's earliest tidal dock.
4. It was discovered in 1954 and excavated in 1955–60 by Mortimer Wheeler.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 4 is wrong: Lothal was excavated by S. R. Rao, not Wheeler. The Bhogava location, the 218 × 37 m sluiced basin and its status as the earliest tidal dock are correct.

s:
Which of the following have been found at Lothal?
1. A ship on a seal and a terracotta ship
2. A Persian Gulf (button) seal
3. A copper dog
4. The Great Granary
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: The Great Granary is at Mohenjodaro. The ship seal, terracotta ship, Persian Gulf seal and copper dog are Lothal finds and show its West Asian trade.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Harappa was a port on the Ravi.
2. Rangpur, Somnath (Prabhas Patan) and Balakot were Harappan ports besides Lothal.
3. The National Maritime Heritage Complex at Lothal is being built by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong: Harappa was an inland city; Lothal was THE port city. Rangpur, Somnath, Balakot (also Kuntasi, Khirasara, Sutkagendor) were ports, and the NMHC (approved Oct 2024) is under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.

s:
Match List-I (Site) with List-II (Excavator):
List-I
A. Harappa
B. Rangpur
C. Rakhigarhi
D. Ropar
List-II
i. Y. D. Sharma
ii. M. S. Vats
iii. Daya Ram Sahni
iv. Amarendra Nath
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Harappa – Daya Ram Sahni (1921), Rangpur – M. S. Vats (1931), Rakhigarhi – Amarendra Nath (1997), Ropar – Y. D. Sharma (1953–56): A-iii, B-ii, C-iv, D-i.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. J. P. Joshi found Dholavira in 1967-68 and R. S. Bisht excavated it in 1990.
2. R. S. Bisht also excavated Banawali.
3. Ropar, on the Sutlej, was the first Harappan site dug after Independence.
4. Mohenjodaro stands on the Ravi.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 4 is wrong: Mohenjodaro is on the Indus; Harappa is on the Ravi. Joshi/Bisht at Dholavira, Bisht at Banawali and Ropar (Sutlej) as the first post-Independence dig are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sohgaura (Gorakhpur) is a Mauryan copper-plate site, not a Harappan one.
2. Kot Diji in Sindh has a pre-Harappan level as well as a Harappan one.
3. Surkotada and Desalpur are Harappan sites in Kachchh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: Sohgaura's copper plate (on famine granaries) is Mauryan; Kot Diji is Harappan and also pre-Harappan; Surkotada and Desalpur are Harappan sites in Kachchh.

s:
Which of the following were found at Mohenjodaro?
1. The bronze Dancing Girl
2. The steatite Priest-King
3. The Pashupati seal
4. The red sandstone male torso
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: The red sandstone male torso is from Harappa. The Dancing Girl, the Priest-King and the Pashupati seal all come from Mohenjodaro.

s:
Match List-I (Find) with List-II (Site):
List-I
A. Camel bones
B. Terracotta toy plough
C. Dog buried with a human
D. Horse bones (doubtful)
List-II
i. Surkotada
ii. Ropar
iii. Kalibangan
iv. Banawali
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Camel bones – Kalibangan, toy plough – Banawali (the ploughed field is Kalibangan), dog with human – Ropar, doubtful horse bones – Surkotada: A-iii, B-iv, C-ii, D-i.

s:
Match List-I (Find) with List-II (Site):
List-I
A. Earliest furnace
B. Rice, bajra and sorghum
C. Ten-sign signboard
D. Bronze chariot
List-II
i. Daimabad
ii. Kot Bala
iii. Rangpur
iv. Dholavira
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Earliest furnace – Kot Bala, rice/bajra/sorghum – Rangpur, ten-sign signboard – Dholavira, bronze chariot – Daimabad: A-ii, B-iii, C-iv, D-i.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Surkotada horse bones are dated c. 2100–1700 BCE.
2. Banawali shows pre-, mature and post-Harappan phases.
3. Cylindrical seals come from Kalibangan and Mohenjodaro, and the ship seal from Lothal.
4. Chanhudaro, the bead-making town, had a fortified citadel.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 4 is wrong: Chanhudaro (bead factory, furnace, ink pot) had NO citadel. The Surkotada dating, Banawali's three phases and the cylinder/ship seal sites are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mohenjodaro means "Mound of the Dead" in Sindhi.
2. Kalibangan means "black bangles".
3. Kotada is the local name of Kalibangan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: Kotada is the local name of Dholavira. "Mound of the Dead" (Mohenjodaro; Lothal means the same in Gujarati) and "black bangles" (Kalibangan) are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan sites and UNESCO:
1. Dholavira (2021) is the only inscribed Harappan World Heritage Site in India.
2. Mohenjodaro was inscribed in 1980.
3. Rakhigarhi is on the World Heritage List, inscribed after Dholavira.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: Rakhigarhi is only on the Tentative List. Dholavira (2021, India's 40th) and Mohenjodaro (1980) are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about Rakhigarhi:
1. It is the largest Harappan site and lies in Hisar, Haryana.
2. Bhirrana, not Rakhigarhi, is regarded as the oldest Harappan site.
3. The dig reported on 23 June 2026 found five complete skeletons and three fragmentary burials.
4. Its Mound 7 cemetery has yielded 156 skeletons.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 4 is wrong: Mound 7 has 56 skeletons. Rakhigarhi (Hisar) is the largest site, Bhirrana the oldest, and the June 2026 dig found five complete skeletons and three fragmentary burials.

s:
Assertion (A): The Rakhigarhi DNA study has been read as a challenge to the Aryan-invasion view.
Reason (R): The ~4,600-year-old female skeleton lacked the "Steppe Pastoralist" gene.
In the context of the above, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Both are true and R explains A: the absence of the Steppe Pastoralist gene was read as indigenous ancestry, which is why the result challenges the Aryan-invasion view.

s:
Assertion (A): Lothal is called the port city of the Harappan Civilisation.
Reason (R): Lothal stands on the Ravi, close to the Arabian Sea.
In the context of the above, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: A is true (tidal dock, warehouse, ship seals) but R is false: Lothal is on the Bhogava near the Gulf of Khambhat; the Ravi is Harappa's river.

s:
Match List-I (Raw material) with List-II (Source):
List-I
A. Tin
B. Gold
C. Lapis lazuli
D. Carnelian
List-II
i. Bharuch / Saurashtra
ii. Badakhshan, via Shortughai
iii. Kolar (Karnataka)
iv. Afghanistan and Iran
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Tin – Afghanistan and Iran, gold – Kolar (also Afghanistan), lapis lazuli – Badakhshan via Shortughai (Afghanistan), carnelian – Bharuch / Saurashtra: A-iv, B-iii, C-ii, D-i.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan metallurgy:
1. Bronze was made by alloying copper with tin.
2. Bronze objects far outnumber pure copper objects.
3. The Harappans pioneered the use of silver, which they imported.
4. The Dancing Girl was cast by the lost-wax process.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: pure copper objects far outnumber bronze ones. Bronze = copper + tin, silver was pioneered (imported from Afghanistan) and the Dancing Girl is a lost-wax casting.

s:
Consider the following statements about early farming sites:
1. Kili Gul Muhammad (c. 5000–4000 BC) is an early farming village of Baluchistan.
2. Lahuradeva (UP) has the oldest paddy according to the latest research.
3. Mahagara is known for early barley cultivation.
4. Koldihwa in the Belan valley was once thought to have the oldest paddy.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: Mahagara is known for rice and cattle pens, not barley. Kili Gul Muhammad, Lahuradeva (oldest paddy) and Koldihwa (once thought oldest) are correct.

s:
Match List-I (Crop) with List-II (Site of evidence):
List-I
A. Wheat (largest finds)
B. Garlic (earliest)
C. Indigo
D. Barley
List-II
i. Rojdi
ii. Banawali
iii. Harappa
iv. Balu
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Wheat – Harappa, garlic – Balu (Haryana), indigo – Rojdi, barley – Banawali: A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii. Garlic is not from Lothal or Rangpur, which gave rice husk.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan crops:
1. Rice husk from Lothal and Rangpur is the earliest in South Asia.
2. Millets and rice were staples at Rangpur and Surkotada.
3. A woven cotton piece was found at Mohenjodaro.
4. The earliest rice cultivation comes from Chanhudaro.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 4 is wrong: the earliest rice evidence is from Lothal and Rangpur, not Chanhudaro. Millets/rice at Rangpur and Surkotada and the Mohenjodaro cotton piece are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Harappans were the first to grow cotton, which the Greeks called Sindon.
2. Sesame and mustard were among Harappan crops.
3. Maize was a Harappan crop.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: maize came with the Portuguese. Cotton (Sindon, from Sindh), sesame and mustard are correct.

s:
Match List-I (Evidence) with List-II (Site):
List-I
A. Terracotta plough model
B. Well irrigation
C. Traces of canals
D. Clay plough
List-II
i. Shortughai
ii. Rakhigarhi
iii. Banawali
iv. Allahdino
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Terracotta plough model – Banawali (also Cholistan), well irrigation – Allahdino (Sindh), canal traces – Shortughai (Afghanistan), clay plough – Rakhigarhi: A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii.

s:
Assertion (A): Harappan farmers practised double cropping.
Reason (R): Canal irrigation is fully proved for Harappan Punjab and Sindh.
In the context of the above, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: A is true but R is false: the notes record double cropping with wooden ploughs and flood irrigation, but canal irrigation in Punjab/Sindh is inconclusive.

s:
Consider the following statements about animals in the IVC:
1. The humped bull (zebu) was the favoured domestic animal.
2. Camel bones have been found at Kalibangan.
3. Horse bones are well established in the early and mature levels.
4. Copper figures of a rhinoceros and an elephant come from Daimabad.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: the horse is not established – no bones or images in the early and mature levels, only doubtful finds. The zebu, Kalibangan camel bones and the Daimabad copper rhino and elephant are correct.

s:
Match List-I (Craft evidence) with List-II (Site):
List-I
A. Ivory, copper and bead workshops
B. Salt production
C. Earliest furnace
D. Black terracotta bangles
List-II
i. Kalibangan
ii. Kot Bala
iii. Kerala-no-dhoro
iv. Kuntasi
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Ivory, copper and bead workshops – Kuntasi, salt – Kerala-no-dhoro, earliest furnace – Kot Bala, black terracotta bangles – Kalibangan: A-iv, B-iii, C-ii, D-i.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan crafts:
1. Chanhudaro, almost wholly a craft town, was a major bead-making centre.
2. Chanhudaro is called the "Lancashire of India" and Lothal the "Manchester of the Harappan civilisation".
3. Specialised shell work was concentrated at Rangpur and Rojdi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: specialised shell work was at Nageshwar and Balakot (also Lothal and Chanhudaro). Chanhudaro's bead-making and the Lancashire/Manchester names are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan contacts with West Asia:
1. Mesopotamian records call the Indus region Meluhha, and Magan is Oman.
2. Sargon of Akkad (c. 2300 BCE) records ships from Meluhha.
3. Harappan seals have been found at Susa, Ur and Nippur.
4. The closest external contact of the Harappans was with Egypt.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 4 is wrong: the closest contact was with Mesopotamia, not Egypt. Meluhha/Magan (Dilmun = Bahrain), Sargon's ships from Meluhha and the seals at Susa, Ur and Nippur are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan foreign trade:
1. Carnelian beads, lapis lazuli and timber were exported.
2. Silver and tin were imported.
3. Woollens were exported.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: woollens were IMPORTED, with silver and tin. Carnelian beads, lapis lazuli, ivory, timber, cotton, copper and gold were exports.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In November 2025 a second Dilmun temple (c. 1900–1800 BCE) was found on Failaka, Kuwait.
2. Dilmun weights followed the Harappan standard.
3. The Harappans had contacts with Altyn-depe in Turkmenistan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: the second Dilmun temple on Failaka (Nov 2025), Dilmun weights on the Harappan standard, and contacts with Altyn-depe (also Shahr-i-Sokhta and Tepe Yahya).

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan internal trade:
1. It was carried on by barter, without metal money.
2. Goods moved in bullock carts with spoked wheels.
3. Kuntasi, Bhagatrav and Prabhas Patan were ports on the Gujarat coast.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: Harappan bullock carts had solid wheels. Barter trade and the Gujarat-coast ports Kuntasi, Bhagatrav and Prabhas Patan are correct.

s:
Assertion (A): Harappa had warehouses but was not a port.
Reason (R): Harappa was an inland city on the Ravi.
In the context of the above, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Both are true and R explains A: Harappa, like Mohenjodaro, had warehouses, but as an inland city on the Ravi it was not a port – the port was Lothal on the Gulf of Khambhat.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan seals and sealings:
1. A sealing is the clay impression of a seal pressed on the knot of a package.
2. An intact sealing showed that the goods were untouched and named the sender.
3. Seals were also used as coins.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: seals served communication, trade, authentication, ownership and as amulets – NOT as coins (the IVC had no coins). Statements 1 and 2 describe sealings correctly.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Pashupati seal:
1. It was found at Mohenjodaro and is made of steatite.
2. The seated figure is ringed by an elephant, a tiger, a rhinoceros and a buffalo.
3. Two deer are shown below the figure.
4. A lion stands beside the figure.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 4 is wrong: the lion is never shown on Harappan seals. The Mohenjodaro steatite seal shows a three-faced horned figure ringed by elephant, tiger, rhinoceros and buffalo, with two deer below.

s:
Match List-I (Seal) with List-II (Find-spot):
List-I
A. Unicorn seal, the first seal found (Cunningham)
B. Seal with a unicorn and script, found abroad
C. Button (Persian Gulf-type) seal
D. Mesopotamian-type cylinder seals
List-II
i. Lothal
ii. Mohenjodaro and Kalibangan
iii. Harappa
iv. Nippur
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: First (unicorn) seal – Harappa (Cunningham, 1872–75), unicorn + script seal – Nippur (Mesopotamia), Persian Gulf button seal – Lothal, cylinder seals – Mohenjodaro and Kalibangan: A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The unicorn is the most common motif on Harappan seals.
2. The pipal is the tree most commonly depicted on seals.
3. The cylindrical steatite seal found at Rakhigarhi in June 2026 carries a tiger motif and ten Harappan characters.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: the June 2026 Rakhigarhi seal has an ALLIGATOR motif and FIVE characters. The unicorn (commonest motif) and pipal (commonest tree) are correct.

s:
Match List-I (Seal shape) with List-II (Feature):
List-I
A. Square
B. Rectangular
C. Mesopotamian-type cylinder
D. Button seal
List-II
i. Persian Gulf type, Lothal
ii. Rare; Mohenjodaro, Kalibangan
iii. Inscription only
iv. Animal motif with inscription
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Square – animal motif with inscription (the standard ~2 × 2 inch steatite seal), rectangular – inscription only, cylinder – rare (Mohenjodaro, Kalibangan), button – Persian Gulf type at Lothal: A-iv, B-iii, C-ii, D-i.

s:
Assertion (A): Most Harappan seals were made of steatite.
Reason (R): Steatite (soapstone) is easy to carve.
In the context of the above, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Both are true and R explains A: seals were mostly of steatite because soapstone is easy to carve (agate, chert, copper, faience, terracotta and ivory were also used).

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan weights:
1. They were mostly of chert, cubical in shape and carried no markings.
2. Lower denominations were binary (1, 2, 4 … 64) and higher ones decimal multiples.
3. The unit weight was about 136.3 g.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: the unit weight was about 13.63 g. Chert cubical unmarked weights and the binary-then-decimal system are correct.

s:
Assertion (A): Harappan trade appears to have been centrally regulated.
Reason (R): Identical weights are found over about 8,00,000 sq km.
In the context of the above, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Both are true and R explains A: the same weights over about 8,00,000 sq km (Dilmun too followed the standard) point to central regulation of trade.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan measuring scales:
1. The ivory scale of Lothal has a smallest division of about 1.70 mm.
2. The shell scale of Mohenjodaro has a unit of about 6.7 mm.
3. The copper scale was found at Lothal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: the copper scale is from Harappa (ivory = Lothal, shell = Mohenjodaro, copper = Harappa). The 1.70 mm and 6.7 mm units are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Harappan script:
1. It is mostly pictographic and the fish is the commonest sign.
2. Boustrophedon writing is reported from Kalibangan.
3. An average inscription has about 5 signs and the longest about 26.
4. About 50,000 inscribed objects are known.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 4 is wrong: about 5,000 inscribed objects (≈3,500 seals) are known. The pictographic nature (fish commonest), Kalibangan boustrophedon and the 5 / 26 sign lengths are correct.

s:
Assertion (A): The Harappan script remains undeciphered.
Reason (R): No bilingual text like the Rosetta Stone has been found.
In the context of the above, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Both are true and R explains A: with no bilingual text and an unknown language, the script cannot be read.

s:
Consider the following statements about readings of the Harappan script:
1. The Proto-Dravidian view, held by Iravatham Mahadevan, Asko Parpola and Father Heras, is the most supported.
2. S. R. Rao read the script as Proto-Dravidian.
3. Bahata Ansumali Mukhopadhyay holds that it is not a language script but tax or trade marks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: S. R. Rao read it as Indo-Aryan (ancestor of Sanskrit), a minority view. Statements 1 and 3 are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Dholavira signboard has ten large signs and was found near the North Gate.
2. The Harappan script was first noticed in 1912.
3. Dholavira was dug by R. S. Bisht from 1990.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: the script was first noticed in 1853; J. Fleet reported seals with unknown symbols in 1912. The ten-sign North Gate signboard and Bisht's 1990 dig are correct.

s:
Match List-I (Burial practice) with List-II (Site):
List-I
A. Extended burials with coffin burial (R-37)
B. Dog buried with a human in an oval pit
C. Pot burials
D. Cemetery of 125 graves aligned north–south
List-II
i. Sanauli
ii. Surkotada
iii. Ropar
iv. Harappa
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: R-37 extended and coffin burials – Harappa, dog with human in an oval pit – Ropar (not Lothal), pot burials – Surkotada, 125 graves – Sanauli (Baghpat, UP): A-iv, B-iii, C-ii, D-i.

s:
Consider the following statements about burials at Harappa and Mohenjodaro:
1. Cemetery R-37 has extended burials with grave goods, the head generally to the north.
2. Cemetery H belongs to the Late Harappan phase and has post-cremation or fractional burials.
3. Fractional burial meant burying the bones after the body had been exposed.
4. Coffin burial is a feature of Cemetery H.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 4 is wrong: the coffin burial belongs to R-37, not Cemetery H. The R-37 extended burials, Late Harappan Cemetery H and the meaning of fractional burial are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Kalibangan has three types of burial.
2. At Kalibangan, circular pits with grave goods but no skeleton have been found.
3. The huddled skeletons at Mohenjodaro are now read as evidence of a massacre.
4. Rakhigarhi's Mound 7 has yielded 56 skeletons, including a ~4,600-year-old woman.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: the huddled skeletons, once read as a massacre, are now read as multiple burials. Kalibangan's three types (incl. skeleton-less circular pits) and Rakhigarhi's 56 skeletons are correct.

s:
Assertion (A): The Harappans believed in an afterlife.
Reason (R): They buried large quantities of precious things with the dead.
In the context of the above, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: A is true – pots, ornaments and copper mirrors were buried with the dead – but R is false: on the whole the Harappans did not bury precious things.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan society:
1. Variation in burial goods and ornament quality is the best sign of social differentiation.
2. Single-roomed barracks have been found at Harappa.
3. Uniform bricks prove differences of social status.
4. There is no proof of a rigid caste system; caste became fixed in the Later Vedic period.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: uniform bricks prove organisation and authority, not status. Burial-goods variation, the Harappa barracks and the absence of rigid caste are correct.

s:
Assertion (A): Harappan ranks and polity can be rebuilt only from material remains.
Reason (R): The undeciphered script gives no names of rulers.
In the context of the above, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Both are true and R explains A: because the script gives no rulers' names, ranks and polity have to be reconstructed from material remains.

s:
Match List-I (View of Harappan polity) with List-II (Based on):
List-I
A. Priestly rule
B. Merchant rule
C. Several rulers / city-states
D. Single state
List-II
i. Most plausible per PMF
ii. Several large cities, no single capital
iii. Trade-driven uniformity, few weapons
iv. Citadels, Great Bath, steatite Priest-King
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Priestly rule – citadels, Great Bath, Priest-King (not conclusive), merchant rule – trade-driven uniformity, city-states – several large cities with no single capital, single state – most plausible per PMF: A-iv, B-iii, C-ii, D-i.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan polity:
1. Uniform pottery, seals, weights, 1:2:4 bricks and grid towns over ~8,00,000 sq km point to a significant authority.
2. The political structure seems corporate, with municipal-type civic administration.
3. Like the Harappans, the Later Vedic people had a corporate polity with a strong Sabha and Samiti.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: the Later Vedic polity was a hereditary monarchy with a weakening Sabha and Samiti. The uniformity over ~8,00,000 sq km and the corporate, municipal-type Harappan polity are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. No royal palaces or temples have been found in Harappan cities.
2. Worship was probably domestic or open-air, and power was not personalised in a king.
3. Public buildings such as the Great Bath and the pillared hall were royal palaces.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: the Great Bath, granary and pillared hall were civic buildings, not palaces. Statements 1 and 2 are correct ("possessed great palaces and temples" is the classic wrong option).

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan dress:
1. Cotton and wool were used, and two garments (upper and lower) were worn.
2. The Priest-King wears a shawl with a trefoil pattern.
3. Stitching of garments is well proved.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: there is no proof of stitching. Cotton and wool, two garments and the Priest-King's trefoil shawl are correct.

s:
Which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched?
1. Lipstick – Chanhudaro
2. Toy factory – Chanhudaro
3. Dice – Harappa and Mohenjodaro
4. Chess-like board game set – Kalibangan
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Pair 4 is wrong: the chess-like game set is from Lothal. Lipstick and the toy factory are Chanhudaro finds and dice come from Harappa and Mohenjodaro; bronze mirrors and ivory combs were also known (iron razors were not).

s:
Assertion (A): The Harappans seem to have been a relatively peaceful people.
Reason (R): Their weapons were few and simple, and they had no horse-drawn chariots.
In the context of the above, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Both are true and R explains A: maces, axes, spears and bows of copper, bronze and stone were few and simple and there were no horse-drawn chariots – hence the peaceful reading.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Dancing Girl:
1. It is about 10.5 cm tall and was found at Mohenjodaro in 1926.
2. It is kept in the National Museum, New Delhi.
3. It is made of bronze, cast by the lost-wax process.
4. In June 2026 NCERT decided to restore its original image in the new Class 12 History textbook.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 4 is wrong: NCERT (18 Jun 2026) is restoring the image in the new Class 9 Art textbook. Its size, 1926 find at Mohenjodaro, National Museum home and lost-wax bronze casting are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan stone sculpture:
1. The Priest-King is a steatite bust of a bearded man in a trefoil shawl with half-closed eyes.
2. The male torso from Harappa is of red sandstone.
3. The Priest-King was found at Harappa.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: the Priest-King comes from Mohenjodaro. The steatite Priest-King's features and the red sandstone (jasper) torso of Harappa are correct.

s:
Assertion (A): Harappan sculpture points to advanced metallurgy and craft specialisation.
Reason (R): Lifelike figures such as the Dancing Girl were cast in bronze by the lost-wax method.
In the context of the above, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Both are true and R explains A: lifelike bronze (lost-wax) and stone figures are the evidence for advanced metallurgy and specialised crafts.

s:
Assertion (A): The male torso of Harappa is not a lost-wax object.
Reason (R): It is carved in red sandstone, not cast in metal.
In the context of the above, which one of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Both are true and R explains A: lost-wax is a metal-casting method (Dancing Girl, Lothal dog and bird, Kalibangan bull); the torso is a stone carving.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan pottery:
1. It was wheel-made, typically red slip with black painted designs; plain red ware was the most common.
2. Its motifs include geometric and floral designs, the pipal leaf and fish-scale.
3. Perforated jars were probably used for straining liquor.
4. Wall paintings are common at Mohenjodaro.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 4 is wrong: the only evidence of Harappan painting is on pottery – no wall paintings. The wheel-made red ware, the motifs and the perforated jars (large hole at the base, small holes in the wall) are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Six types of pottery have been reported from Kalibangan.
2. A painted jar from Lothal shows the cunning fox story.
3. Big Harappan storage jars reached Egypt.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: big storage jars reached Oman, not Egypt. Kalibangan's six pottery types and Lothal's cunning-fox jar are correct.

s:
Arrange the steps of the lost-wax (cire perdue) process in the correct order:
1. Molten metal is poured into the hollow mould.
2. A wax model is coated with clay.
3. The clay is removed.
4. The mould is heated and the wax melts out.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Wax model coated with clay (2) → heated, wax melts out (4) → molten metal poured into the hollow mould (1) → clay removed (3): 2, 4, 1, 3.

s:
Match List-I (Metal object) with List-II (Site):
List-I
A. Bronze dog chasing a deer
B. Copper dog and bird
C. Bronze bull / ox
D. Chariot group, buffalo, rhinoceros, elephant
List-II
i. Daimabad
ii. Kalibangan
iii. Lothal
iv. Harappa
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Dog chasing a deer – Harappa, copper dog and bird – Lothal, bronze bull – Kalibangan, chariot group and animals – Daimabad: A-iv, B-iii, C-ii, D-i.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Lost-wax casting continued in the Daimabad bronzes and later in Chola bronzes such as the Nataraja.
2. Rakhigarhi has yielded a gold foundry with an active furnace.
3. Gold and silver necklaces come from Allahdino.
4. The chariot group, buffalo, rhinoceros and elephant of Daimabad are of bronze or copper.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: All four are correct: lost-wax lived on in the Daimabad and Chola bronzes; Rakhigarhi had a gold foundry; Allahdino gave gold and silver necklaces; the Daimabad figures are bronze/copper.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan terracottas:
1. Heavily jewelled female figurines from Harappa are identified as the Mother Goddess.
2. Toy carts with seated drivers come from Chanhudaro.
3. Terracottas were refined objects reserved for the upper class.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: terracottas were crude and used by common people as toys or cult objects; seals and metal images were for the upper class. Statements 1 and 2 are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Chanhudaro had a bead-making factory with a furnace and a shell-ornament factory.
2. Chanhudaro is the only Harappan city without a citadel.
3. Rakhigarhi had a gemstone factory with more than 3,000 semi-precious stones.
4. Lothal had no bead workshops.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 4 is wrong: Lothal had bead workshops and exported carnelian beads. Chanhudaro's bead and shell factories, its lack of a citadel and Rakhigarhi's gemstone factory are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about faience:
1. It is made of ground sand or silica glazed blue-green.
2. It is called the world's first glazed ware.
3. Its tie with mosaic glass is an early clue to glass-making.
4. It was used only for making seals.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 4 is wrong: faience was used for beads, bangles and tiny vessels. Its make-up, its title as the first glazed ware and the mosaic-glass clue are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan beads:
1. Carnelian came from Saurashtra / Bharuch.
2. Beads were exported to Mesopotamia and the Persian Gulf.
3. Iron was one of the bead materials.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: iron was unknown; beads were of carnelian, agate, jasper, steatite, lapis lazuli, faience and gold. Statements 1 and 2 are correct.
